The new cases: a 59-year-old man in Qianzhen District infected with Dengue Virus Type II, diagnosed after three medical visits with the infection source under investigation; and a 59-year-old woman in Gushan District infected with Dengue Virus Type I, linked to an existing cluster. - WHO staff evacuated from Akwe hospital in Ituri Province, Democratic Republic of the Congo, after sheltering there for three days amid heavy fighting. Staff from WHO and DR Congo’s health ministry left the hospital and were temporarily relocated until security improves. Ituri is the epicenter of a deadly Ebola outbreak caused by the Bundibugyo variant; there are currently no vaccines or treatments for this variant. The conflict has hindered the response across eastern and northeastern DR Congo. The outbreak has reached 11,762 cases and 5,775 deaths, the worst on record for DR Congo. Two candidate vaccines targeting Bundibugyo are planned to enter clinical trials in Ituri. The 1.5 million doses would secure supply, but three gates separate doses from patients: trial results, WHO expanded-access guidelines for unapproved vaccines, and undisclosed delivery funding. - Ebola virus disease (EVD) in North Kivu, Democratic Republic of the Congo, saw two survivors discharged from the Ebola Treatment Centre at Beni General Referral Hospital on Nov 24, 2026, including the outbreak’s first pregnant woman cured. The pregnant patient arrived early after developing symptoms, was isolated, tested positive, and transferred to the ETC for close medical care, with gynecological supervision aiding her recovery. The evacuation marks ongoing gains in patient outcomes at a center operated by the International Medical Corps. As of Nov 20, 2026, at least 143 people had recovered from EVD at the Beni ETC. Authorities emphasize early case detection and prompt treatment, and appeal for community support to sustain progress and vigilance against the Ebola outbreak.
- Ebola in Kisangani, the capital of Tshopo Province in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, faces response challenges due to community insecurity after an Ebola response worker was assaulted and died. The deceased, attacked in Bafwasende Territory last October, died on Sunday after transfer to Kabondo General Referral Hospital in Kisangani. The incident highlights a two-pronged crisis: the Ebola virus disease (EVD) outbreak and escalating community atrocities that hinder response efforts. Early yellow fever symptoms include sudden fever, headache, muscle and back pain, nausea, vomiting; progression can include jaundice, dark urine and bleeding. Vaccination is recommended for everyone aged nine months and above in affected districts; routine nine-month vaccination should be ensured. Meningitis risk rises; seek care for fever, headache or neck stiffness. Authorities await laboratory confirmations; GAPHTO calls for strengthened surveillance, timely sample transport, and frontline worker safety.
